name: Nanyang Technological University
feeMethod: Undergraduate tuition is one rate for almost all degrees (Business/Accountancy and Medicine differ). Master's use each programme's own fee, less any subsidy for Singaporeans and PRs.
description: Nanyang Technological University is a public research university established in 1991, with roots in Nanyang University (1955) and the Nanyang Technological Institute (1981). whyIncluded: One of Singapore's MOE-funded Autonomous Universities and, with NUS, one of the two comprehensive local universities that most Singaporean students weigh against overseas options.

programmes.notes: Self-financed programme; the page states students are not eligible for MOE subsidies. Minimum total tuition (30 AUs) incl. 9% GST for admission in AY2027 (from Aug 2027): S$58,403.07; AY2026: S$56,156.80. Published as one figure for all nationalities, so the international tier is the fee everyone pays (incl. 9% GST). No current Citizen/PR tier (re-checked 2026-10-02): the page's 'SC/SPR Incentive' and 'MSc Programme Financial Support' sections, the NTU Graduate Admissions financial-matters page (/admissions/graduate/financialmatters/ntupgi) and coursework admission guide (/admissions/graduate/cwadmissionguide), the School's MSc brochure PDF and the EEE MSc FAQ state the S$5,000 NTU subsidy for Singaporeans/PRs in self-financed master's by coursework programmes only 'from the academic year starting in 2024' and 'for academic year starting in 2025'; no NTU statement was found that it continues for the AY2026/27 or AY2027/28 intakes, so no SC/PR fee is derived for those intakes. History: the AY2025 intake total is from the Wayback Machine capture of this page dated 2 Jun 2025 (web.archive.org timestamp 20250602151144), which states 'From August 2025 Intake Onwards ... Minimum Total Tuition Fees (30 AUs): SGD$56,156.80' incl. GST and, on the same page, that the S$5,000 SC/PR subsidy applies for the academic year starting in 2025; the 2025 citizen and pr rows are DERIVED as S$56,156.80 - S$5,000 = S$51,156.80 (deducted from the GST-inclusive total). AY2024 intake: no source states the 2024 total, so no 2024 rows are recorded. The earliest archived capture of the financial-matters page is the June 2025 one above; 2024 captures of the EEE MSc landing page, FAQ and NTU's central programme pages could not be retrieved (the current versions link to the financial-matters page rather than quoting fees), the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2024-25 coursework fee PDF lists only MOE-subsidised programmes, and aggregators (libertify, collegedunia) quote only AY2026/AY2027 figures. Excludes miscellaneous fees (S$610 full-time for AY2025). Citizen/PR rates for the AY2026 and AY2027 intakes (added 2026-10-04 at the site owner's direction): the international total minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy for Singaporeans and PRs in self-financed master's by coursework, deducted from the GST-inclusive total as for the AY2025 rows (AY2026: 56,156.80 - 5,000 = 51,156.80; AY2027: 58,403.07 - 5,000 = 53,403.07). Basis: NTU's Post-graduate Incentives page (linked from the EEE financial-matters page) describes the subsidy as continuing, with eligibility rules stated 'for students from AY2025 intake onwards' and no end date. Note that the page's subsidy sentences name only the 2024 and 2025 academic years explicitly, and the EEE MSc brochure of 10 Sep 2026 lists a single AY2027 fee without mentioning the subsidy, so confirm with eee_mscadmission@ntu.edu.sg before relying on the Citizen/PR figure. AY2024 intake (found 2026-10-05 in Common Crawl): NTU's central programme pages for the EEE self-financed MSc programmes carry the fee block that the EEE financial-matters page did not have archived for 2024. The Common Crawl captures of ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/master-of-science-in-electronics (CC-MAIN-2024-10, 2024-03-02; CC-MAIN-2024-26, 2024-06-17), .../master-of-science-in-signal-processing (CC-MAIN-2024-22, 2024-05-25) and .../master-of-science-in-power-engineering (CC-MAIN-2024-26, 2024-06-19) all state, for the five EEE self-financed MSc programmes including Communications Engineering: 'Important Updates: Below table for intakes starting from August 2024. Per Course: S$4,883.20* Per Dissertation: S$9,766.40* Minimum Total Tuition Fees: S$48,832*', '*Inclusive of 9% GST from 1 Jan 2024', one figure for all nationalities, plus 'All Singapore Citizens (SC) and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR) will be eligible to receive a S$5,000 subsidy'. An earlier capture (signal-processing, CC-MAIN-2023-50, 2023-11-30) gives the same August 2024 table before GST (S$4,480 per course, S$44,800 minimum total, '#Exclusive of 9% GST'); 44,800 x 1.09 = 48,832, consistent. The Dec 2024 to Jun 2025 captures replace it with the 'From August 2025 Intake Onwards' S$56,156.80 table already recorded. Rows: international = S$48,832 (30 AUs, 1-year programme, incl. 9% GST, same basis as the current record); citizen/pr DERIVED as 48,832 - 5,000 = S$43,832, deducted from the GST-inclusive total as for the 2025-2027 rows; here the subsidy is stated on the same page for that intake (and NTU's 2025 pages say it applies 'from the academic year starting in 2024'). The intake is August 2024, so feeYear 2024. Excludes the S$5,000 deposit (offsets tuition) and miscellaneous fees. Source is the official NTU page as archived by Common Crawl (WARC records read directly from data.commoncrawl.org), so it can stay sourceType 'official' with the archive noted. For reference only (not recorded): pre-August-2024 intakes paid the 'admission from AY2020 onwards' per-nationality table, minimum total S$32,700 (SC) / S$38,150 (SPR) / S$43,600 (international) incl. 9% GST from 1 Jan 2024. Fix 2026-10-15: the 2024 rows' source https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/master-of-science-in-electronics now redirects to the renamed MSc in Integrated Circuits and Microelectronics page, so they point instead at the sibling EEE programme page https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/master-of-science-in-signal-processing (still live, no redirect), whose Common Crawl capture of 25 May 2024 (CC-MAIN-2024-22) carried the identical 'intakes starting from August 2024' fee table (S$48,832 minimum total incl. 9% GST, S$5,000 SC/SPR subsidy) already cited above; figures unchanged. Fix 2026-10-15: GST uncertainty resolved, figures confirmed. The EEE financial-matters page states every fee '*Inclusive of Goods and Service Tax (GST)' (9% from 1 Jan 2024) and NTU's Post-graduate Incentives page says the S$5,000 subsidy 'will be disbursed proportionally across the duration of the coursework programmes, to offset the tuition fees charged for each respective semester/trimester', i.e. a flat S$5,000 credited against the GST-inclusive bill, not a before-GST reduction (NTU marks the only before-GST concession, the alumni 10% rebate, as such on the CCDS fee schedule). The 2024-2027 citizen/PR rows (GST-inclusive total minus S$5,000) therefore stand. Sources: https://www.ntu.edu.sg/eee/admissions/programmes/graduate-programmes/msc/financial-matters and https://www.ntu.edu.sg/admissions/graduate/financialmatters/ntupgi (read 2026-10-15).

programmes.name: MSc in Artificial Intelligence (MSAI)
programmes.feeBasis: The published AY2027 total for the one-year MSAI (incl. GST). Citizen/PR figures are estimated: the published S$5,000 NTU subsidy plus S$5,000 school study grant are taken off; international students pay the full total.
programmes.summary: Total tuition for the one-year programme, including 9% GST. Citizen/PR figure is the international fee less a S$5,000 NTU subsidy and a S$5,000 school study grant. Miscellaneous fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme, not MOE-subsidised. Total tuition incl. 9% GST for AY2027/28 and after: S$65,748.80 (12 months minimum full-time), published as a single figure for all nationalities; the international tier is that figure. NTU publishes no net Singapore Citizen/PR fee (checked 2026-10-01: the programme page, its FAQ, the CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF and the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2026-27 coursework fee PDF, which lists only MOE-subsidised programmes). The citizen and pr tiers are DERIVED: S$65,748.80 total minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy the page states for 'Singaporeans and permanent residents who enrol in self-financed master's by coursework programmes at NTU' (section 'Financial Assistance (AY2025 intake onwards)') minus the additional S$5,000 CCDS study grant the page states for 'all Singaporeans and permanent residents' 'starting from AY2026 intake' = S$55,748.80. They are flat dollar amounts deducted from the GST-inclusive total. Excludes the means-tested top-up (up to S$15,000 for those needing financial aid) and the 10% NTU alumni rebate. History from the official CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF linked from the page ('Past Tuition Fees'): AY2025 and AY2026 intakes S$63,220 (all nationalities, incl. 9% GST); the SC/PR history rows for those intakes are derived the same way from that PDF, which states the S$5,000 NTU subsidy 'from AY2025 onwards' for SC and PR, the S$5,000 CCDS study grant for Singaporeans 'starting from AY2025 intake' and for PRs 'starting from AY2026 intake': AY2026 SC and PR S$63,220 - 5,000 - 5,000 = S$53,220; AY2025 SC S$53,220, PR S$63,220 - 5,000 = S$58,220. AY2024 intake had separate published rates, SC S$39,785, PR S$47,415, international S$59,187 (all incl. 9% GST). Excludes miscellaneous fees. Fix 2026-10-15: GST uncertainty resolved, figures confirmed. The CCDS MSc tuition fee schedule PDF states 'All fees listed are in Singapore dollars (S$) and inclusive of Goods and Services Tax (GST)' (9% for AY2024 onwards, 8% for AY2023, 7% for AY2019-22 tables), that the S$5,000 SC/PR subsidy 'will be distributed evenly across the entire billing period' and the S$5,000 CCDS study grant 'will be applied on the second payment of the course', while it marks only the alumni rebate as '10% off the tuition fees (before GST)'; the MSAI page likewise says '*All fees shown are inclusive of 9% prevailing GST' and that 'study grants and other incentives will also be applied to these two instalments'. So the subsidy and grant are flat amounts credited against the GST-inclusive instalments and the derived 2025-2027 citizen/PR rows stand. Sources: https://www.ntu.edu.sg/media/docs/librariesprovider118/pg/ccds-msc-tuition-fees-schedule31b2bfac-f5a2-4aae-aec3-071337b13505.pdf?sfvrsn=b0ad6e18_1 and https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/master-of-science-in-artificial-intelligence (read 2026-10-15).

Citizen/PR DERIVED: the NBS Fees & Funding page states that Singapore Citizens and PRs admitted to the full-time Nanyang MBA get a study grant of 10% of the tuition fee, so the SC/PR figure is 90% of the published fee: S$92,955.20 x 0.9 = S$83,659.68 incl. GST (equivalently S$85,280 - S$8,528, plus 9% GST). Nanyang MBA ... S$ 75,000*' with '*Published tuition fee excludes prevailing GST set at 9%', and the Fees & Funding page captured 25 Jun 2024 (timestamp 20240625211650) gives the GST-inclusive fee schedule (enrolment fee S$21,800 + S$5,450 + S$27,250 + S$27,250 = S$81,750, 'includes prevailing GST rate') and the same 10% SC/PR study grant, so the 2024 international row is S$81,750 and the 2024 citizen/pr rows are DERIVED as 90% = S$73,575. 2025 intake (August 2025) added 2026-10-04 from the Wayback Machine capture of NBS's admissions page dated 9 Dec 2025 (timestamp 20251209043701, read through the translate.goog mirror of web.archive.org): 'AY2025 (August 2025 intake) ... Nanyang MBA, 12 months, Singapore, S$ 82,000' with '*Published tuition fee excludes prevailing GST set at 9%', so the 2025 international row is S$82,000 x 1.09 = S$89,380 incl. GST (the same total NBS's Fees & Funding schedule shows for the AY2026 intake, capture 20260418074853: enrolment fee S$21,800 + S$7,994.06 + S$29,792.97 + S$29,792.97 = S$89,380; the admissions page still showed the AY2024 table in its 27 May and 15 Jun and 8 Sep 2025 captures, and NTU's programme page went from 'Academic Year 2024: S$81,750' in its Jan-Jul 2025 captures to '2026 Intake: S$89,380' by Oct 2025 without ever printing a 2025 label). The 2025 citizen/pr rows are DERIVED as 90% = S$80,442, applying the 10% study grant for Singapore Citizens/PRs on the full-time Nanyang MBA that NBS's Fees & Funding page states in its 25 Jun 2024 capture and its Apr 2026 capture ('Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents of Singapore admitted to the full-time Nanyang MBA are eligible for a study grant of 10% of the tuition fees'); that page has no 2025 capture and the Dec 2025 admissions page does not mention the grant, so the 2025 SC/PR rows assume the grant ran unchanged between those two captures. programmes.summary: Total fee for the one-year programme, including 9% GST. Citizens get a S$10,900 study grant and PRs S$5,450 off the published fee. Miscellaneous and application fees are extra.
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme (listed under NTU's non-subsidised coursework programmes). One-year full-time programme taught over three trimesters, so the total programme fee is the annual fee (divided by durationYears 1). The SPMS programme page publishes one tuition fee for all nationalities per intake, incl. 9% GST: AY2027/28 S$64,841.92; AY2026/27 S$62,348.00; AY2025/26 S$59,950.00; the international tier is that figure. Citizen/PR DERIVED (re-verified 2026-10-01): the same page's 'Financial Assistance' section states that Singapore Citizens enjoy a study grant of S$10,000 + prevailing GST (S$10,900) and Singapore PRs S$5,000 + prevailing GST (S$5,450), applied evenly across the trimesters, so the current (AY2027/28) tiers are S$64,841.92 - S$10,900 = S$53,941.92 for citizens and S$64,841.92 - S$5,450 = S$59,391.92 for PRs (both incl. GST). The grant statement carries no intake year and the page says grants are reviewed annually, so it is applied only to the current published fee; the 2026 and 2025 history rows for citizens and PRs record the published total for everyone, not a derived net fee. AY2024 intake (added 2026-10-02) from the Wayback Machine capture of this page dated 21 Jul 2024 (timestamp 20240721112827): 'The tuition fees for Academic Year 2024/25 are as follows: Tuition Fee (inclusive of GST) S$55,000 + prevailing GST (S$ 59,950)' (international row); that capture also gave a payment schedule by nationality for AY2024/25 (deposit S$5,450 + first payment S$24,525 for all, then second payment S$19,075 for Singapore Citizens, S$24,525 for PRs and S$29,975 for international students, i.e. the SC S$10,900 and PR S$5,450 study grants already applied), so the 2024 citizen row is S$49,050 and the pr row S$54,500, the totals of that schedule. Excludes the means-tested financial aid (up to S$10,900 more for needy SC/PRs), the 10% NTU alumni grant, the S$50 application fee and the yearly one-time miscellaneous fee.

programmes.notes: New self-financed full-time coursework master's from the School of Social Sciences, first intake August 2026 (NTU news release 27 Jan 2026: 1.5 years, 5 trimesters incl. 500 practicum hours; tracks Community Health Psychology, Neuropsychology, Thanatology, Forensic Psychology). MScP 'Tuition Fees & Scholarships' page (read directly 2026-10-05): tuition for all students irrespective of nationality S$68,175 (AY2026) and S$70,905 (AY2027), covering the entire 18-month programme, incl. GST, payable in five equal trimester instalments. feeYear 2027 uses the AY2027 figure: S$70,905 / 1.5 = S$47,270 (international tier); AY2026 history row S$68,175 / 1.5 = S$45,450. Citizen/PR: the same page states 'All Singapore Citizens (SC) and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR) are eligible for a tuition fee subsidy of up to S$5,000', so the SC/PR tiers are DERIVED as total minus S$5,000, deducted from the GST-inclusive total as for NTU's other self-financed master's entries, then divided by 1.5: AY2027 (70,905 - 5,000) / 1.5 = S$43,936.67; AY2026 (68,175 - 5,000) / 1.5 = S$42,116.67.
